title: The derived category of modules on a ringed space has products
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and let $D(\mathcal O_X)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then every family $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ of objects of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ indexed by a set $I$ has a product $\prod_{i\in I}K_i$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-category-product]; in particular $D(\mathcal O_X)$ has countable products.

source.place: Tag 07D9, label lemma-derived-products (for a Grothendieck abelian category; sheaves of modules on a ringed space form one, Remark Tag 079Q, label remark-existence-D)

proof.text: Apply the Grothendieck-abelian conclusion of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to the small site of opens of X and its structure sheaf. The source-library instance CategoryTheory.Abelian.hasKInjectiveResolutions_of_isGrothendieckAbelian supplies K-injective resolutions. Module sheaves have all limits, so the proved source-library instance DerivedCategory.hasLimitsOfShape_discrete supplies products for every indexing type in universe u, including the empty type. This is exactly HasProducts.{u}.
